landmarks.name: Ethnographic Museum (Pristina)
landmarks.writeup: A museum showcasing traditional Kosovar culture, crafts, and lifestyle.

landmarks.name: Visoki Denani Monastery
landmarks.writeup: A 14th-century Serbian Orthodox monastery, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

landmarks.name: Germia Park
landmarks.writeup: A large national park near Pristina, popular for hiking and outdoor activities.

landmarks.name: Newborn Monument
landmarks.writeup: A symbol of Kosovo's independence, unveiled in 2008 in Pristina.

cultural_events.name: Dokufest
cultural_events.writeup: An international documentary and short film festival held annually in Prizren.

cultural_events.name: Pristina Jazz Festival
cultural_events.writeup: A yearly event attracting international jazz musicians to Kosovo's capital.

food_writeup: Kosovar cuisine blends Balkan and Mediterranean influences, featuring dishes like flija (layered pancake), burek (filled pastry), and tavë kosi (baked lamb with yogurt).
brief_history: Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008 following years of conflict and UN administration after the 1998-1999 Kosovo War. It is recognized by over 100 countries but not universally.
current_conflicts: Tensions persist between Kosovo and Serbia, particularly in northern Kosovo where ethnic Serbs reside. Diplomatic efforts continue to normalize relations.
